answer: At the harbor ledger, Quiet Forge records every first delivery as a public beacon, then inks that beacon onto one page of a shared atlas that only an already-established neighbor may countersign. A second claimant for the same atlas page collides on the inked beacon and is turned away. A sybil farm would have to fund a real first delivery and recruit a fresh established countersigner for each fake berth, so minting identities is no cheaper than doing the work.
